units.translation: Of the forms of this verb, which have been discussed by Choeroboscus in Theodos. p. 886 and in Thes. vol. 7 p. 2163 and by Veitch (Greek verbs irregular and defective p. 561 ff. 3rd ed.), Aeschylus uses these: present indicative τίθημι [I place], τίθησι [he places], τιθεῖσι [they place] (Ionic for τιθέασι [they place] Ag. 465), imperative τίθει [place], subjunctive τιθῶ τιθῆς [I place, you place], participle τιθείς τιθεῖσα τιθέντες τιθεῖσαι [placing (masc. sg.), placing (fem. sg.), placing (masc. pl.), placing (fem. pl.)], first aorist ἔθηκα ἔθηκας ἔθηκε [I placed, you placed, he placed], second aorist ἔθεσαν [they placed], imperative θές and θέντων [place (sg.), let them place], optative θείη [he might place], infinitive θεῖναι [to place], participle θέντα θέντες θεῖσαι [having placed (masc. sg.), having placed (masc. pl.), having placed (fem. pl.)], future θήσω θήσει θήσομεν [I will place, he will place, we will place], infinitive θήσειν [to be about to place], participle θήσων [about to place]. Of the middle forms τίθεμαι [I place for myself] he uses the present imperative τίθου [place for yourself], aorist ἔθου ἔθεσθε ἔθεντο [you placed for yourself, you placed for yourselves, they placed for themselves], optative θεῖτο and plural θείατο [he might place for himself, they might place for themselves] (Suppl. 694), subjunctive θώμεθα [let us place for ourselves], infinitive θέσθαι [to place for oneself], future θήσομαι θήσει θησόμεσθα θήσονται [I will place for myself, he will place for himself, we will place for ourselves, they will place for themselves].
There are few examples of compounds προστίθημι [I add] and συντίθημι [I put together].
I place.
I establish.
I make, I cause.
With an infinitive
With an adjective, participle, or noun, I render.
Middle form τίθεμαι [I place for myself] I place, I make, I provide.
I hold for myself, I win for myself.
Perfect passive τεθειμένος [having been placed] Suppl. 186 is corrupt for τεθυμμένος [having been burned], which Abresch restored. See τύφω [I burn].
Thus Hermann for μεθήσομεν [we will let go].
Thus Hermann for εὐφήμοις μοῦσαι θεαί τ᾿ ἀοιδοί [with auspicious Muses and goddesses, singers].
I pray that I will set up trophies.
But will Zeus ever set up trophies of these evils?
Where on earth shall we place him?
He places the leashes on their necks.
Do not place your foot on the ground.
He places his foot upright or covered.
Before placing foot on this muddy land.
I place these things in the midst of the evil curse,
But before the enemies, place, Zeus, the one from within the halls.
I will establish this law for all time.
Answer word for word, placing each in turn.
He turns all other things upside down and places them.
And these branches on other altars – place them.
I will place this pig, very well-fed, in the roaring oven.
As you command, we will do all these things for the gods.
They made everything utterly bad.
Care will set the rest aright.
We will make them rule this house well.
How can I be blameless in your eyes?
Do not cause harm.
Having established common contests.
Do not make delay.
Raise a cry, setting a song together.
Making a kick of the dinner as a just requital.
But still, if a god wishes, he might make from these more melodious sounds.
We will establish a woven lament as the city's custom.
Causing bloody ruin.
They are about to bring destruction upon the house of Agamemnon.
Making paths despondent and routes ill-omened.
Having brought destruction upon the city.
Having caused these scattered flights for the citizens.
He made peace for all his friends.
Many wrestling bouts – about to set for the Danaans.
Did he not also bring deceitful ruin upon his house?
Having established that learning through suffering holds authority.
Since Zeus made you, without anger, a partner in the lustral waters for the house.
